FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} seared one minute a side, with {1_coll} cut into batons and fried twice in {2_plur} — once low, to cook them through, once very hot, to colour them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole piece of {0_adj} cooked on its bone and carved in front of you. The flesh against the bone is the best of it, and the last to be served.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached then napped with a sauce mounted with {1_plur} and scattered with {2_adj} fried apart, so that they do not give up their water into the sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} browned under a {1_adj} and {2_adj} sauce. The story goes that the wife of the mayor of Dijon knocked the paprika tin over the dish and improvised the rest.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} taken in {1_plur} without colour, moistened to the top, the sauce thickened at the last with {2_adj} yolks that must not be allowed to boil again.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} shank
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the small muscle of the shank, braised so long that it slides off the bone. One shank a guest, never fewer.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: best-end chops grilled two minutes a side, rubbed with {1_plur} and finished with {2_plur}. Eaten by the bone in the hand, once the fork has been given up.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} jointed and fried, then stewed with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, deglazed with white wine and lifted with tarragon.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: game {0_coll} marinated three days, braised with whole {1_coll}, the sauce thickened with the blood and the crushed liver. Blacker and stronger than that of the farmed rabbit.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} of black game marinated a week in {1_plur} and juniper, braised until it falls into threads, the sauce bound with blood.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an old bird, too tough to roast, braised buried under {1_coll} and smoked {2_coll} until it gives way. The cabbage takes on all the taste of the game.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an escalope of {0_adj} fried and deglazed with cider, with {1_coll} taken in butter and a {2_adj} sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} in cubes browned then stewed with {1_plur} and {2_plur}. Improvised, they say, on the evening of the battle, from whatever Bonaparte's cook could find in the fields around.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a roast of {0_adj} sliced and then rebuilt, each slice parted from the next by a {2_adj} and onion purée, the whole napped with {1_plur} and browned. Created for a Russian prince posted to Paris.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: thin escalopes of {0_adj} rolled around a {1_adj} stuffing, tied and braised with {2_coll}. They were called headless larks, until people looked at them a little more closely.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} hollowed out, salted and turned over to drain, stuffed with minced {1_plur} and {2_plur}, baked on a bed of rice that drinks up the juices.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} split and hollowed, the flesh taken out and chopped with {1_coll} and put back inside, the whole browned with {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} beheaded and emptied of their seeds, filled with {1_plur} and half-cooked {2_plur} — it will swell in the oven and pull the skin tight.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole cabbage blanched and opened leaf by leaf, packed with {1_plur} between every layer, then closed up in a cloth and poached for hours. It is cut into wedges, like a cake.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: an assortment of small vegetables — {0_coll}, {1_coll} and their flowers — hollowed and stuffed, packed tight into a dish and cooked together in olive oil. Eaten warm rather than hot.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} blanched in salted water and drained a long while, then napped with a {1_adj} béchamel and browned with {2_plur}. Badly drained, the gratin gives up its water and falls apart.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} split in four and washed down to the last grain of sand, melted in butter then drowned in {1_plur} and browned with {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in butter with a pinch of sugar to cut the bitterness, rolled up in {1_plur}, napped with béchamel and browned with {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} broken into buttered ramekins on a bed of {2_adj}, a spoonful of {1_adj} over the top, cooked in a water bath until the white sets and the yolk stays liquid.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} barely beaten, poured into foaming {2_plur} and stirred fast, rolled while still running in the middle. Parsley, chervil, chives and tarragon: four herbs, no more and no fewer.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} fried apart until every drop of their water has gone, slipped into {0_coll} at the moment of rolling the omelette.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} sweated down until they turn almost translucent, bound with {1_plur} beaten with {2_plur}, in a case blind-baked in advance.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {0_adj} galette filled with {2_plur}, {1_plur} and cheese, the four corners folded into a square around the yolk left whole.
